slots.title: Trump order widens tax-exempt diesel
slots.body:
U.S. President Donald Trump signed an executive order Monday to expand access to tax-exempt diesel.

Oil-linked markets were already moving in the cross-asset tape before the open narrative shifted to equities and data.

slots.title: World Bank East Asia growth 4.5%
slots.body:
The World Bank lifted its 2026 growth forecast for East Asia and the Pacific to 4.5%.

The bank said AI-related goods drove more than half of export growth in most of the region’s economies.

It also warned about AI concentration risks as those exports dominate the growth story.

U.S. participants were already looking ahead to American data — including August trade figures due later Tuesday, per early-week currency commentary.

Does a 4.5% regional growth print change how you read U.S. export demand from Asia?

slots.title: U.S. session recap — Oct. 6, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,773.95, up 51.23 points from the prior close of 7,722.72, with an intraday range of 7,727.59 to 7,794.35.

The Nasdaq Composite added 1.1% to 27,477.31; the session high was 27,544.06, matching the year high in the injected index data.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.2% to 51,267.90, while the Russell 2000 rose 0.5% to 2,847.14.

Among Nasdaq sectors in the bundle, Industrials averaged about +4.0%, Utilities about +2.1%, and Consumer Cyclical about +1.7%; Real Estate was roughly flat at -0.2%.

Large tech and chip names contributed to the tone:
- $NVDA +2.1% to 238.90
- $AVGO +2.1% to 362.51
- $META +1.9% to 741.90
- $GOOGL +0.9% to 346.47

$TSM closed up 2.8% at 485.80 with a 487.44 session high; payment networks $V (+2.5%) and $MA (+2.2%) also finished firmly green.

Brazil and LatAm exposure stood out in volume leaders:
- $EWZ +12.5%
- $NU +13.0%
- $BBD +18.6%
- $ITUB +15.5%

$WBD was heavily traded at 30.95, essentially unchanged at 0.0%.

On the downside among liquid names, $RZAI was -35.1% to 12.91; $RPM, on a scheduled report date in the calendar, fell 3.9% to 95.30.

The calendar listed Oct. 6 earnings for $STZ, $RPM, $LW, and $BLLN with estimates only in the feed — no reported actuals were injected for this recap.

Cross-asset: the VIX rose 1.4% to 15.52; gold futures (GCUSD) slipped 0.2% to 4,148.90; Brent crude (BZUSD) rose 0.6% to 100.97 while the USO ETF was -2.3% at 143.99; the UUP dollar fund gained 0.3% to 28.99; Bitcoin was -0.2% at 85,569.59.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-10-02 in the data showed a 10-year yield at 5.3% and a 2s10s spread of 0.45 percentage points.

Overseas indexes in the bundle included the Nikkei 225 +0.8%, Hang Seng +0.7%, and FTSE 100 +0.3%.

The U.S. economic calendar entry for the session was the October Economic Optimism Index (estimate 44.5, previous 45.6, low impact) — no other major prints were listed in the injected calendar for this close.
